newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's deputy PM sees 250,000 new jobs in '97.
newsitem.headline: Spain's deputy PM sees 250,000 new jobs in '97.

text.p: Spain's deputy Prime Minister Francisco Alvarez Cascos said on Thursday that unemployment would fall by another 250,000 people in 1997.

"If 1996, which was a difficult year, ended with a fall in unemployment of 160,000 people...the improvement in expectations for the Spanish economy in 1997 suggests that we can reduce unemployment by another 250,000 people," he told state radio in an interview.
The number of registered unemployed fell by 160,859 people to 2.21 million in 1996.
Cascos' forecast was slightly more optimistic than that predicted by Spanish Labour Minister Javier Arenas in December who said 237,000 new jobs would be created in 1997.
Cascos added that labour reform was now vital and trade unions and businessmen must agree on measures to modernise the economy.
"Everything is not resolved and now, trade unions and businessmen have a responsibility to make advances in this direction," he said.
"Spanish companies must become as competitive as their European rivals and as part of this, businessmen and trade unions are discussing how they can modernise the economy," he added.
Cascos said he was optimistic for 1997.
"Indicators for 1997 do not point to a mere transitory recovery, but we are on the brink of a new stage in the Spanish economy," he said.
